To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dielectric permittivities of anodised titanium oxide thin films decrease in the initial stage of their growth, and that the evolution of the permittivity during anodisation is related to the growth morphology of these films.
the dielectric permittivities of TiO(2), ZrO(2) and Ta(2)O(5) films grown by anodisation can be monitored in real time by measuring the evolution of electrostatic stresses developing in the films.

the evolution of the permittivity of anodized oxide films can be followed in-situ, and that this evolution can be explained in terms of changes in the morphology of the oxide films during anodization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of capacitance-based microsensors for the detection of DNA hybridisation.
the synthesis of anodic oxide thin films with a high dielectric permittance, which is an essential requirement for the development of capacitance-based microsensors.
the preparation of thin films of high permittivity for use in capacitance-based DNA sensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dielectric permittivities of the films were found to decrease with time during the first growth regime and reach a constant value during the second growth regime, which is consistent with a change in growth mechanism from a columnar to a more compact growth structure.
the dielectric permittivities of anodised oxide films are strongly influenced by their growth morphology, which is determined by the anodising electrolyte, current density and time.
the in-situ monitoring of dielectric and electrostriction properties of the anodised films has been achieved by using a novel method, which is based on the measurement of electrostatic stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dielectric properties and the growth morphology of TiO(2), ZrO(2) and Ta(2)O(5) anodised oxide thin films can be followed in real time during the anodisation process.
the electrostrictive stress developing in the oxide film during anodisation can be used as a tool for following the dielectric and morphological evolution of the oxide.
the electrostrictive properties are not constant and that they depend on the film thickness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dielectric permittivities of anodic TiO2, ZrO2 and Ta2O5 thin films can be controlled by controlling the growth morphology of these films.
the dielectric and piezoelectric properties of anodic TiO2 films can be controlled during growth by tuning the anodisation conditions.
the evolution of the film morphology during anodisation is the main factor governing the evolution of the effective dielectric permittivities of anodic oxide films.
